paper_metadata.title: Encoding of Probability Distributions for Quantum Monte Carlo Using Tensor Networks

experiments.description: Univariate log-normal distribution loading and approximation with TT-cross, including scalability analysis over qubit count and bond dimension, plus a 5-qubit hardware execution on IBM Eagle R3.

algorithm.variant: TT-cross tensor-train probability loading mapped to quantum circuits via TT-to-unitary decomposition

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A univariate continuous log-normal distribution is discretized into 2^d points and encoded on d qubits as amplitudes; TT-cross is used to approximate the discretized probability vector before mapping to a quantum circuit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate the target discrete probability distribution p(x_i) with a tensor-train representation and encode it into a quantum state whose amplitudes match the distribution.

problem_instance.description: Univariate log-normal distribution calibrated from real market data for financial instrument pricing.

dataset_specification.description: Log-normal parameters calibrated using real market data from Itaú Unibanco; no ticker symbols or date range reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Continuous distribution discretized into a binary grid; probability vector normalized to sum to 1.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: KS distance versus target distribution across qubit counts; average training time versus qubit count; circuit depth comparison against Qiskit built-in LogNormal implementation; hardware run on 5 qubits with 10,000 shots; IBM hardware results compared under optimization levels 1 and 3.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: TT-cross approximation used to construct the tensor-train representation; TT cores reshaped and decomposed by SVD; circuit built with Qiskit UnitaryGate.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement-based empirical distribution estimation and comparison to target distribution using KS distance.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: training time scales logarithmically with number of points; precision degrades beyond 15 qubits in some settings

classical_baselines.value: linear in number of discretization points
linear in number of discretization points

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation / QMC in general
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes this speed-up has been questioned because query complexity may not reflect total computational complexity, and state preparation overhead can negate the advantage.

speedup_claims.factor: better circuit-depth scalability than Qiskit built-in method
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the TT method scales linearly in circuit depth, while the Qiskit method scales exponentially in qubits.

speedup_claims.conditions: with respect to number of discretization points
speedup_claims.caveats: Training time is reported to scale logarithmically with the number of points; precision degrades beyond 15 qubits in some settings.

scalability_data.metric_value: run on IBM Eagle R3 with 10000 shots
some patterns of the expected distribution preserved
distribution appears more uniform; significantly worse

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Circuit depth and operation complexity scale logarithmically with system size for the TT-cross approach; circuit depth scales linearly with number of qubits in the reported comparison.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Qiskit/Grover-Rudolph state preparation scales linearly with the number of discretization points, implying exponential scaling in qubit count.

experiments.description: Bivariate log-normal distribution loading and approximation using TT-cross with mirroring quantization, evaluated by KL divergence and training time.

algorithm.variant: TT-cross tensor-train probability loading with mirroring quantization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two-dimensional log-normal distribution is discretized and encoded using mirrored binary ordering so that the most significant qubits of each variable are adjacent.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate the bivariate target distribution with a TT representation and encode it into a quantum state.

problem_instance.description: Bivariate log-normal distribution calibrated from real market data for financial pricing.

dataset_specification.description: Two-dimensional financial distribution from Itaú Unibanco; no explicit asset names or date range reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Mirroring quantization used to order qubits; distribution discretized per dimension.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: KL divergence versus target discrete distribution and average training time as a function of qubits per dimension.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: TT-cross approximation followed by mirroring quantization and TT-to-circuit mapping via SVD-based decomposition.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: KL divergence computation and training-time measurement.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: training time scales well with qubits per dimension

speedup_claims.conditions: for bivariate log-normal distributions using mirroring quantization
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide exact numeric KL values in text; results are shown in Figure 8.

speedup_claims.factor: training time scales well with qubits per dimension
speedup_claims.caveats: No exact timing numbers are reported in the text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Reported circuit depth scales linearly with number of qubits in the TT approach.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Qiskit built-in LogNormal implementation scales linearly with discretization points.

experiments.description: Higher-dimensional multivariate log-normal distribution loading and approximation using TT-cross with interleaving quantization, evaluated up to five dimensions.

algorithm.variant: TT-cross tensor-train probability loading with interleaving quantization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Multivariate distributions are discretized and encoded by interleaving qubits from different variables to preserve correlations across dimensions.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Approximate the target multivariate distribution with a TT representation and encode it into a quantum state.

problem_instance.description: Multivariate log-normal distributions up to five dimensions, interpreted as up to five assets.

dataset_specification.description: Financial distributions from Itaú Unibanco; up to five dimensions and up to ten qubits per dimension, yielding up to 250 discretization points.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Interleaving quantization used to arrange qubits across variables; distributions discretized per dimension.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: KL divergence and average training time as a function of qubits per dimension; simulations only for higher-dimensional cases.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: TT-cross approximation followed by interleaving quantization and TT-to-circuit mapping via SVD-based decomposition.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: KL divergence computation and training-time measurement.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: training time exhibits a logarithmic pattern

classical_baselines.value: linear in number of discretization points

speedup_claims.conditions: higher-dimensional multivariate log-normal distributions up to five dimensions
speedup_claims.caveats: KL divergence is reported as relatively low, around 10^-2 in the worst case; exact per-point values are not provided in text.
The paper only explicitly shows circuit-depth scaling for 2D and 3D cases in Figure 10.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Reported training complexity scales logarithmically with the number of discretization points; circuit depth scales linearly with number of qubits in the TT approach.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Qiskit built-in method scales linearly with the number of discretization points.
